answer: An attacker who spins up many fake identities must fund every one, and losing any challenge forfeits the bond to the challenger, making mass fakery costly. A concrete sybil-resistance mechanism is stake-bonded identity anchoring: each agent must lock a refundable bond before voting or earning rewards, and peers challenge suspicious duplicates by posting a matching bond. Honest participants keep their bond as a haven of reputation, while the challenge pool flows like a river of escrowed funds, and the locked stake acts as an anchor tying each identity to real economic risk.
